title: What is IAM? 🔐
description: Learn the role of AWS Identity and Access Management and why it's the cornerstone of cloud security.

slides.title: The Gatekeeper of Your AWS Kingdom 🏰
slides.content:
# AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)

IAM is a **global service** that controls **who** can do **what** on your AWS resources. It answers two questions:
- **Authentication**: Who are you? (Identity)
- **Authorisation**: What are you allowed to do? (Permissions)

Every action in AWS – launching an EC2 instance, reading a file from S3, shutting down a database – goes through IAM. If IAM says no, it doesn't happen.

**Analogy**: IAM is like the security badge system in a high‑tech building. Your badge proves your identity (authentication), and the zones you can enter depend on your clearance level (authorisation).

quizData.question: What two fundamental questions does IAM answer?
quizData.explanation: IAM handles authentication (who) and authorisation (what they can do).

slides.title: IAM is Global 🌍
slides.content:
# No Region Selection Required

Unlike EC2 or S3, IAM is a **global service**. You set it up once, and it works across every AWS Region.

- An IAM user created in the `us-east-1` console can still launch resources in `eu-west-2`.
- Policies and roles are global as well.

This simplifies security management: you don't have to duplicate users per region.

slides.title: The Root User vs IAM Users 👑
slides.content:
# The Ultimate Power

The **root user** is created when you sign up. It has unrestricted access to everything. Using it for daily work is dangerous.

**IAM users** are individual identities you create with specific permissions. They start with **zero permissions** – you must explicitly grant everything.

> Never use the root account except for a few tasks (e.g., changing billing details, closing the account). Even for admin work, create an IAM admin user.

slides.title: ⛔ Root Account Danger
slides.content:
## The Root Account Has All Keys

* Can delete all your resources, including backups.
* Can close the entire AWS account.
* Can change billing information.

**Protect it with MFA and lock the credentials away.** Create an IAM admin user for yourself immediately.

quizData.question: Which of the following can only be performed by the AWS root account?
quizData.explanation: Only the root account can close an AWS account. Everything else can be delegated to IAM users with proper permissions.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Free to Use 🚀
slides.content:
## IAM is Free

IAM itself costs nothing. You can create as many users, groups, and roles as you want. The only charges are for the resources those identities consume.
